_comment: Scopes present in scope-allowlist.ts (via the rawapi source) that the Feishu/Lark developer console rejects with 'permission does not exist' on bulk import. Excluded from the console-import list embedded in docs/app-setup_{en,zh}.md. Ground truth is a real bulk-import into a test app: an earlier round accepted all 226 others and rejected exactly the entries below, and the two im:message:* entries were confirmed on the lark-cli 1.0.88 list. The four scopes added at 1.0.89 were confirmed accepted on the 233-entry list: base:template:read and im:chat.membership_application:read/write imported as new, and im:message:update was already granted. Capabilities are unaffected — coarse :write scopes and correctly-spelled variants remain in the allowlist. Re-verify after each lark-cli bump (see docs/skills/bump-lark-cli.md Step 6c).

misspelled_or_aggregate._comment: Not real console permission points — wrong spelling or a bare aggregate. Correct forms remain in the list (e.g. bitable:app, im:resource, mail:user_mailbox:readonly, calendar:calendar:readonly). For the two im:message entries: the console grants the coarse im:message / im:message:readonly and the per-chat-type im:message.group_msg:get_as_user / im:message.p2p_msg:get_as_user, but not a bare im:message:basic or im:message:get_as_user. They reach the allowlist only as alternative scopes listed by the read-receipt raw APIs (im/messages/read_status and read_users). Since lark-cli 1.0.89 those endpoints also have first-class shortcuts (im +messages-read-status / +message-read-users) whose preflight scope is the grantable im:message:readonly, so the capability is reachable and dropping these two from the import list costs nothing.

task_fine_grained._comment: Fine-grained task actions the console folds into the coarse task:*:write (which remains). Exception: task:personnel:writeonly has no coarse counterpart, but no user-facing tool depends on it — it is rawapi-only.

whitelist_gated._comment: Real scope but whitelist-restricted; ordinary apps cannot request it. The lark_slides_screenshot tool maps to wiki:node:read via shortcut, not this scope, so dropping it costs nothing.
